title: Universal holonomic control of algebras of observables
abstract: Closed paths of observable algebras can enact logical gates. We show that algebras of fixed block structure have a unique unitarily invariant parallel transport, recovering Berry--Wilczek--Zee transport on bands. On positive-dimensional configuration spaces, the holonomy group is the special-unitary part of the normalizer: every inner logical gate and every equal-type sector permutation is attainable. Given a compatible gapped Hamiltonian and access to the required paths, inner logical gates can be implemented adiabatically by isospectral control of a band refinement.
summary: This paper develops a geometric theory for controlling quantum systems by analyzing the parallel transport of observable algebras along closed paths. It proves that this holonomy mechanism can universally implement all necessary logical gates and sector permutations. This establishes a rigorous link between the geometry of the observable space and the computational power of the quantum system.
main_problem: The paper addresses the geometric problem of determining how observable algebras must be transported (parallel transported) when the algebra itself undergoes a closed path evolution in the space of observables.
main_result: It shows that the parallel transport is uniquely fixed by unitary invariance, recovering Berry–Wilczek–Zee transport, and that closed paths can realize every inner logical gate and sector permutation on positive-dimensional strata.
method: The analysis employs geometric control theory, defining a canonical connection and calculating the holonomy group associated with the evolution of the observable algebra structure.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum states described by observable algebras $A$, analyzed using the Artin–Wedderburn decomposition. The control is achieved via paths in the space of these algebras, often related to band structures derived from gapped Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Holonomy ($	ext{hol}(\gamma)$), inner logical gates, sector permutations, and the curvature $F(\mu)$ of the connection.
important_parameters: The structure of the algebra (fixed block structure $	au$), the existence of a compatible gapped Hamiltonian, and the path taken ($\gamma$).
main_assumptions: The results are derived for algebras with a fixed block structure, and the adiabatic implementation relies on the existence of required control paths.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the concept of holonomy for a closed control loop, showing how the failure of the lifted frame to close results in a non-trivial holonomy element belonging to $N(A)$.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the geometric problem of transport on observable algebras, deriving the canonical connection, calculating the holonomy for closed loops, and finally proving that these holonomies realize universal gates under adiabatic control.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep geometric framework connecting the algebraic structure of quantum observables to the realizable unitary operations, offering a powerful tool for designing quantum gates.
